title: Does Lamarckian inheritance compound the learning bias across generations?
question: In Experiment N (not pre-registered as a hypothesis), Lamarckian populations attacked 2-3x more and went extinct in 9/16 runs vs 2/16 Darwinian. Inheriting learned weights may pass on the locomotion weakening found in I-K, so it accumulates over generations. Does that replicate on fresh seeds, and does a stimulus-specific critic (which should remove the bias) prevent it?
background: share_gene is the inborn mean weight into 'share' divided by the inborn mean weight into locomotion; a rise means inherited wiring shifts toward social actions. The state critic is the intervention from Experiment R (critic='state'). Static world, viscous. Seeds 1300-1311 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Lamarckian populations go extinct more often
Inherited wiring shifts toward social actions under Lamarckian inheritance
A state critic lets Lamarckian populations survive longer
A state critic reduces the inherited shift toward social actions
